cues.en: It's time for another bleeding edge alert.
cues.zh: 又到了前沿研究提醒。

cues.en: This is where we talk about some recent research that has promising results but hasn't made it into the mainstream with recommender systems yet.
cues.zh: 這裡介紹近期一些結果很有潛力，但尚未成為推薦系統主流的研究。

cues.en: I want to mention an interesting paper from the 2017 Conference on Recommender Systems.
cues.zh: 我想介紹 2017 年推薦系統研討會的一篇有趣論文。

cues.en: It's called Translation-based Recommendations, and it comes from a team at the University of California at San Diego.
cues.zh: 它叫做 Translation-based Recommendations，來自加州大學聖地牙哥分校的團隊。

cues.en: If you want to check out the original paper as well as the data and code behind it, you can find it at this link.
cues.zh: 如果想看原始論文，以及背後的資料與程式碼，可以從這個連結找到。

cues.en: The idea behind it is that users are modeled as vectors moving from one item to another in a multidimensional space.
cues.zh: 概念是，把使用者建模成多維空間中，從一個項目移動到另一個項目的向量。

cues.en: And you can predict sequences of events, like which movie a user is likely to watch next, by modeling these vectors.
cues.zh: 透過這些向量建模，就能預測事件序列，例如使用者接下來可能看哪部電影。

cues.en: The reason this paper is exciting is because it outperformed all of the best existing methods for recommending sequences of events in all but one case in one data set.
cues.zh: 這篇論文令人興奮，是因為在事件序列推薦上，除了某個資料集中的一種情況外，都勝過當時所有最佳方法。

cues.en: And I also like that they measured their results based on hit rate instead of accuracy.
cues.zh: 我也喜歡他們根據命中率，而不是準確程度衡量結果。

cues.en: They are focused on the right thing.
cues.zh: 他們專注在正確的事情上。

cues.en: This image from the paper illustrates the basic idea.
cues.zh: 論文中的這張圖，說明基本概念。

cues.en: You position individual items, like movies, in a transition space, where neighborhoods within this space represent similarity between items, so items close together in this space
cues.zh: 將電影等個別項目，放進一個轉移空間，空間中的鄰域代表項目相似度，因此位置接近的項目，

cues.en: are similar to each other.
cues.zh: 彼此相似。

cues.en: The dimensions correspond to complex transition relationships between items.
cues.zh: 各維度對應項目間複雜的轉移關係。

cues.en: Since this technique depends on arranging items together into local, similar neighborhoods, I still classify it as a neighborhood-based method.
cues.zh: 因為這個技術仰賴將項目安排到局部相似鄰域，我仍把它歸類為鄰域式方法。

cues.en: In this space, we can learn the vectors associated with individual users.
cues.zh: 在這個空間中，可以學習與個別使用者相關的向量。

cues.en: Maybe a user who watches a Tom Cruise movie is likely to move along to the next Tom Cruise movie, for example, and that transition would be represented by a vector in this space.
cues.zh: 例如，看過一部 Tom Cruise 電影的使用者，可能接著看下一部 Tom Cruise 電影，這個轉移就用空間中的向量表示。

cues.en: We can then predict the next movie a user is likely to watch by extrapolating along the vector we've associated with that user.
cues.zh: 接著，沿著與該使用者相關的向量外推，就能預測他接下來可能看的電影。

cues.en: The paper doesn't go into a lot of detail on how it's done, but they do provide the code and data they used, so if you can read C++ code, you can reverse engineer what they did.
cues.zh: 論文沒有詳細說明做法，但提供了程式碼與資料，因此如果能讀 C++，就能反向分析他們做了什麼。

cues.en: It's all very advanced stuff, but it seems to work.
cues.zh: 這些都相當進階，但似乎有效。

cues.en: So if you find yourself in a situation where you need to predict a sequence of events, like which movies or videos a person is likely to watch next given their past history,
cues.zh: 因此，如果需要預測事件序列，例如根據歷史，預測某人接下來可能看哪部電影或影片，

cues.en: you might wanna do a search for translation-based recommendations and see how it's coming along in the real world.
cues.zh: 可以搜尋「平移式推薦」，看看它在真實世界的發展。

cues.en: Mainly, I just want you to remember the term translation-based recommendations, so you can remember to check up on it if you need to recommend sequences some day.
cues.zh: 主要是希望你記得 Translation-based Recommendations 這個詞，將來需要推薦序列時，就記得查查。

cues.en: Right now, it's bleeding edge, but it looks promising.
cues.zh: 目前還是前沿技術，但看來很有潛力。
